channel.title: The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (occrp.org)

item.title: Ukraine Charges Ex Energy Minister with Money Laundering in ‘Operation Midas’ Case
item.description: NABU investigators allege the former energy minister used two shell companies to funnel millions in illicit funds to his family in Switzerland as part of the 'Operation Midas' probe.

item.title: Bank Documents Expose Scale of Secret Investments in Adani Group by Adani Family Associates
item.description: As the massive conglomerate faced allegations of market manipulation, two men who had close ties to the Adani family, including appearing as directors in affiliated companies, held billions in Adani stock.

item.title: Anti-Corruption Probe Launched Into Romanian Business Registry’s Failed IT System
item.description: Romania’s 38 million-euro business registry IT system, blocked for weeks in 2024 and now operating with intermittent failures, is under an anticorruption probe following audits revealing mismanagement and security lapses.

item.title: Cyprus Court Acquits Ex-Parliament President, MP in Golden Passport Case
item.description: Cyprus court clears ex-Parliament president, MP in a case linked to golden passports, citing missing witnesses and lack of evidence.

item.title: Made in the EU, Dropped on Kyiv: How European Parts Are Enabling Russia’s Winter Drone War
item.description: The workhorse of Russia’s drone fleet — responsible for crippling Ukraine's energy grid and triggering a humanitarian crisis — is built with EU technology. Despite tightening sanctions, parts for the Geran-2 are still flowing into Russia with ease.

item.title: Russian Man on U.K.’s Most Wanted List Holds Maltese ‘Golden Passport’
item.description: British authorities allege that Alexander Kuksov, a Russian with Maltese citizenship, was part of a major money laundering operation. His brother was convicted for his role in the same network.

item.title: Five Questions on Mexican Cartel Drones
item.description: Vanda Felbab-Brown, a scholar of international organized crime, discusses the specter of violent conflict between Mexican cartels and the current U.S. administration.

item.title: Following OCCRP and Partners Investigation, Ireland Will “Pursue” Issue of Irish Components in Russian Drones
item.description: Ireland discusses investigation that found despite EU sanctions prohibiting direct exports to Russia, components produced by European companies — including those from Ireland — are ending up in Russian drones

item.title: Seven Years Before Beirut Explosion, Lebanese Military Failed to Flag Deadly Cargo
item.description: The MV Rhosus was allowed to sail into Beirut’s port carrying 2,750 tons of potentially explosive ammonium nitrate, even after an inspection by the Lebanese navy, documents show. Lebanon's Armed Forces failed to include the inspection in a report submitted to the government after the blast.

item.title: Peru Congress Ousts Interim President Ahead of Election
item.description: Peru Congress Ousts Interim President Ahead of Election
